newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.

text.p: * French President Jacques Chirac is expected to arrive in Bucharest this afternoon on a two-day official visit.

* France supports Romania's early admission to NATO on grounds that is meets compatibility criteria required for alliance membership, a spokesman for the French presidency told a news conference in Paris. Chirac's visit will open a new era of French-Romanian relations, the spokesman said.

* Chirac will be accompanied by Foreign Minister Herve de Charette, Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre and by Finance & Foreign Trade Minister Yves Galland. French MPs and businessmen will also be part of Chirac's delegation.
* France is Romania's most solid support for its bid to achieve integration into western structures, president Emil Constantinescu said in an interview to Romanian state radio.
He said he pleaded for a new approach to boost trade between the two countries.
* Romanian politicians hailed Chirac's visit and its importance in light of France's historic role in supporting Romania's interests:
- Paris is Romania's first and best advocate, Senate chairman Petre Roman said.
- The most important aspect for Romania is France's plea for all NATO candidates to start membership talks at the same time, Foreign Minister Adrian Severin said.

- Romania owes France much of its post-communist victories in foreign diplomacy, former Foreign Minister Teodor Melescanu said in a reference to the Council of Europe, the European Community and the European Union. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
